your_book:
Monday was a split-session story for Jaleel's book. The winners were loud: Vertex Pharma surged 5.6%, Expand Energy added 5.1%, and Uber gained 4.0% — the latter likely lifted by broader macro optimism even as the K-shaped economy debate simmered in the headlines. Zoetis (+3.0%), Adobe (+2.9%), and Boston Scientific (+2.3%) also contributed meaningfully, and the NVIDIA-linked $500B AI financing consortium headline gave that name a tailwind in the news cycle, though the stock itself slipped 2.9% on the day — a reminder that good stories don't always translate to green closes. ServiceNow rode the software sector's Palantir-led sentiment bid for a +2.1% session.

The drag came from the book's single largest position: RKLB fell 3.4% and now sits with a paper gain of only 2.1% despite commanding 15.6% of the book. That weight-to-performance mismatch is uncomfortable, and the AVOID verdict from the model makes it the most glaring drift in the portfolio — price holding up thinly while the thesis says exit. NVDA's 2.9% drop, despite the consortium headline, also deserves scrutiny; export-control risk hasn't gone away and earnings are due August 26. AZO dipped 1.9% and remains barely above water overall (+0.5% total gain), a quiet underperformer for a STRONG BUY-rated name.

Watch list into the week: BSX carries an elevated risk flag (FY26 guidance cut to 7–8.5% growth, flat through Q3 guided) yet still gained 2.3% today — the market may be pricing in a recovery that management hasn't confirmed. LULU continues to flatline with Americas comps down five straight quarters; its next catalyst isn't until September 2. The book's overall unrealized gain of 7.64% is real but concentrated in a handful of compounders — ABT, NOW, and DHR — while several positions are effectively underwater or treading water.

attention.headline: Largest position, AVOID verdict, thin gain — size vs. conviction mismatch is acute
attention.note: At 15.6% of the book with only a 2.1% total gain and a model verdict of AVOID, today's 3.4% drop sharpens the question of why this remains the single largest weight in a capital-preservation portfolio.

attention.headline: Stock fell 2.9% despite blockbuster AI consortium headline — earnings in 16 days
attention.note: The disconnect between a headline $500B AI financing deal and a negative session close suggests the market is pricing export-control risk ahead of the August 26 earnings report, which is the next hard catalyst.

attention.headline: Elevated risk flag persists — FY26 guidance cut, flat Q3 guided, yet stock rallied today
attention.note: Today's 2.3% gain runs counter to management's own flat-through-Q3 guidance; if the market is getting ahead of a recovery that hasn't been confirmed, the next earnings (Oct 20) could reset expectations sharply.

attention.headline: Five straight quarters of negative Americas comps, margins under tariff pressure, flatline total return
attention.note: With a HOLD-QUAL verdict, a guidance cut on record, and the next read not until September 2, there is no near-term catalyst to close the gap between a stagnant price and a deteriorating fundamental picture.
